name: Review (v2, on the crawl's building blocks)
description: (#2310 P4c/P4c-2, NOT the frozen `review` id) A code review built as a SECOND mission config on the crawl's shared blocks (#2301/#2310), never as a fork of it: `plan-<rule>` mints one `plan.sites` task per rule with `source: "diff"` (the DIFF-scoped strategy on the same plan_sites pattern `crawl.plan`'s tree walk uses — see plan_sites_step.rs); `unit-<rule>` GROWS one `crawl.unit` dispatch per planned site, `role_id: "reviewer"` (the SAME step kind crawl.json's `unit-<rule>` phase uses, generalized in this packet to read the Task's own role rather than a hardcoded `crawler`); `create-mods` reuses crawl's create-mod pattern (plus its own `gate-step`, #2310 P4c-2b) over this run's own findings; `deliver` (#2310 P4c-2b) gathers this run's own finding/mod stores and renders a GitHub review payload. Crawl never learns what a PR is (DESIGN.md): this document names no crawl MISSION-CONFIG id and `crawl.json` is untouched by this packet, but it does name two of crawl's STEP KINDS by their current ids — `crawl.unit` and `crawl.summary` — because that is where the shared blocks live today. The vocabulary is the leftover, not the coupling: P4d folds both into mission-agnostic kinds, and this document's step `kind` fields change with them. (#2310 fix-loop C2) `outcome_from: "deliver"` names what this run DELIVERS rather than inheriting the positional 'last phase's last task' guess: the `mission close` payload is the deliver step's own DeliverOutcome, and a run whose delivery task itself errored exits 1 instead of 0.

inputs.name: workspace
inputs.description: Path to a workspace spec JSON naming the checked-out tree at the diff's own head — REQUIRED for every `plan-<rule>` step. Unlike the frozen `review` config's `worktree`/`github` inputs, a diff-scoped plan step reads through `workspace_spec::materialize`, the SAME mechanism `crawl.json` uses, so this run needs a real materialized source (a `path` source pointing at the checked-out tree is the common case — see the P4 brief's own live-plumbing-proof recipe, "over a tempdir tree of the post-diff fixture"). Must resolve to exactly ONE source.

inputs.name: diff_file
inputs.description: Path to the unified diff this review plans against. Canonicalized at step-config parse time.

inputs.name: intent_file
inputs.description: Path to the PR body / intent text `intent-vs-diff` compares the diff against. Mirrors the frozen `review` config's own input of the same name. READ, on every unit dispatch: each `unit-<rule>` task grows `"intent_file": "{{intent_file}}"` into its `crawl.unit` step's config, `UnitStepConfig::from_step` parses it (unit_step.rs L823-828, empty string filtered to absent so a launch that passes no `intent_file` is not a path-read failure), `run` reads the file (L1092) and `build_message` renders its text ahead of the window as "The stated intent for this change (a PR body or intent file) is:" (L342-345). Leave it unset and `intent-vs-diff` has nothing to compare the hunk against, so it reports nothing — the rule runs, sees no stated intent, and every unit it planned comes back empty.

inputs.name: head_sha
inputs.description: The diff's own head sha — mirrors the frozen `review` config's input. Reaches each `plan-<rule>` step's config but is not yet consumed (see `plan_sites_step.rs`'s module doc: `Plan.sources[0].sha` comes from the checked-out tree today, not this param).

inputs.name: github
inputs.description: owner/repo — mirrors the frozen `review` config's input. Reaches each `plan-<rule>` step's config but is not yet consumed (no fetch path exists yet — see `plan_sites_step.rs`'s module doc).

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Mirrors the frozen `review` config's input. Accepted for CLI-surface parity; not yet read by any step in this document.

inputs.name: bundler
inputs.description: Mirrors the frozen `review` config's input (the external-bundler plugin path). Accepted and IGNORED (#2310 P4c-2 item 4: declared "ignored" structurally, not detected by config id) — `review-v2` does not use the funnel's bundler; its planner reads `diff_file` directly. Passing it prints a named warning at launch time (before dispatch, on the `--dry-run` path too) saying it is ignored, so an operator carrying a `bundler=` param over from a `review` launch line gets a visible signal rather than a silent no-op.
inputs.ignored_reason: review-v2 does not use the funnel's bundler; its planner reads diff_file directly

inputs.name: envelope_out
inputs.description: Mirrors the frozen `review` config's input. Still NOT consumed (#2310 P4c-2b): `deliver.github_review` writes the rendered `{mode, review}` payload only (via `emit`), never a separate full envelope file — there is no envelope shape in this document's own pipeline for this to name.

inputs.name: emit
inputs.description: Path to write the rendered `{mode, review}` payload the `deliver` phase's `deliver-step` produces. `-` (or omitted) writes to stdout, matching the frozen `review` config's own `emit` contract.

inputs.name: attribution
inputs.description: Attribution text for the posted footer, threaded to the `deliver` phase's `deliver-step` — mirrors the frozen `review` config's own `attribution` input. Absent means no footer line (`deliver.github_review`'s own default), NOT the frozen config's envelope-derived default — this document has no member-record envelope to derive one from.

inputs.name: test_command
inputs.description: The gate command `create-mods` runs against a proposed mod before counting it confirmed (#2310 P4c — DESIGN.md "the changed files name the test targets"). Wired (#2310 P4c-2b): the `create-mod` task's `gate-step` (`mods.gate`) takes `{{item.tree_root}}` as its `workdir` and, for every mod naming the finding the task addresses, resolves the single source checkout beneath it, copies that checkout to a scratch dir, `git apply`s the mod's kit there, and only then runs this command INSIDE the patched copy (mods_gate.rs L193-202, L266-269, L305-306) — never in `tree_root` and never in the read-only source itself, so a gate can never mutate the tree a finding was observed in. `tree_root` is where the checkout is resolved FROM, not where the command runs. Each mod is recorded `gate_passed`/`gate_skipped_reason`. Leaving it unset means every mod is recorded `gate_skipped_reason: "no test_command configured"`, never gate-verified — and the visible consequence in the delivered review (#2310 fix loop A, S1-5) is that NO suggestion block is ever rendered: `deliver.github_review` turns a mod into a one-click suggestion only when its gate PASSED, so with no `test_command` every mod-form finding delivers as a "Worth a double check" thread instead.

inputs.name: rules
inputs.description: Comma-separated rule ids to review with, same selection mechanism as `crawl.json`'s own `rules` input — a `plan-<rule>` task whose rule is not named is pruned at mint with reason `not_selected`. Absent means every enabled plan task this document declares.

inputs.name: draws
inputs.description: How many times to dispatch each planned unit (#2310 P4c-2b — DESIGN.md "a draws-per-unit knob, off by default, ports the measured k-draw recall technique from the funnel"). Absent means 1 (`crawl.unit`'s own default) — one dispatch per unit, unchanged from before this input existed. `finding_refs` dedup on `(rule, file, line)` across a unit's own draws before `create-mods` grows from them, so a duplicate observation across draws never mints two coder tasks for the same window.

inputs.name: review-probe-high
inputs.description: Seat override for the `unit-<rule>` tasks — same param name shape the P4 brief's live-plumbing-proof recipe uses (`--param review-probe-high=probe-4b`), kept even though this document has no probe/judge/verify staffing split of its own YET: a single seat resolves every `unit-<rule>` task via the `reviewer` role's own `role_profiles.reviewer` binding, or this override.

inputs.name: dry_run
inputs.description: The generic `mission launch --dry-run` flag, injected by the CLI layer. Prints the task/step graph this launch would mint and mints nothing.

inputs.name: mod_wait_seconds
inputs.description: How long the `create-mods` phase waits, per finding, for a frontier-written mod to appear in the mod store. **Default `0`, which means DO NOT WAIT**: the wait step completes immediately with `{"waited": false, "found": false, ...}`, the gate finds no mod, and `deliver.github_review` renders that finding as a question, exactly as it does today. That is the honest behavior on the UNATTENDED path (the self-hosted runner running `darkmux-review.yml`): no orchestrator session is watching the hook there and the runner has no frontier seat, so a per-finding wait would be pure wall-clock. An ATTENDED run opts in with `--param mod_wait_seconds=<N>`, N being the window the operator's monitor + the `darkmux-mod-create` skill needs to record a mod. Poll cadence is ~5s, so the effective wait rounds up to a multiple of 5. **Keep N below `runtime.step_command_timeout_seconds`** (env `DARKMUX_STEP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default 600): that is the bound `procedural.shell` applies to EVERY step command, it is the outer bound here, and if it is the smaller of the two it kills the poll first and the step errors naming it rather than naming this input. **A wait that ends with NO mod is a CLEAN outcome, not an error** (#2310 P4e review): the step exits 0 with `{"waited": true, "found": false, ...}`, the gate records its ordinary no-mod skip and the finding delivers as a question. A frontier that reads a finding and declines to write a mod — a search-form finding, or one that does not hold — is doing the RIGHT thing, and erroring there would finalize every such run Degraded. Only a non-numeric `mod_wait_seconds` (exit 2, a real config defect) and an infra failure error the step.

inputs.name: mod_seat_profile
inputs.description: The endpoint profile the OPTIONAL `create-mod-dispatch` template staffs its `coder` seat with (#2310 P4f) — an unattended alternative to `create-mod`'s bounded wait, for the self-hosted runner where no orchestrator session exists to receive the create_finding hook. Names a profile in `~/.darkmux/profiles.json` whose model declares an `endpoint` (xAI, Google Gemini and OpenAI are all OpenAI-compatible; the key lives in a macOS Keychain item the profile's `endpoint.auth.keychain` names, never in the config). Reaches the dispatch as the step's `profile_name`, the same override `dispatch.internal` reads from a Task or a step config. **Only read when `create-mod-dispatch` is ENABLED** — the template ships `"enabled": false` and is pruned at mint, so on a default launch this input is inert. Leaving it UNSET while the template is enabled is also legal and is the other way to staff the seat: a declared-but-uncollected whole-value placeholder omits its key entirely, so no `profile_name` reaches the step and the dispatch resolves `coder` through the machine's own `role_profiles.coder` binding. **Data boundary:** a hosted endpoint sees the finding and the source it names — public repositories only.

phases.description: One planning task per rule, diff-scoped. Each materializes `workspace`, reads `diff_file`, and writes plan/<rule>.json — the SAME `Plan` content shape `crawl.plan` writes (`plan.sites`'s tree-source path IS `crawl.plan`'s own `plan_one_rule`), just produced from a diff's hunks instead of a tree walk.

tasks.description: Plan the `intent-vs-diff` rule over the diff.
Plan the `existing-solution` rule over the diff.
Plan the `shared-symbol-callers` rule over the diff.
Plan the `union-vs-enum` rule over the diff.
Plan the `test-gap` rule over the diff.
Plan the crawl's `swallowed-error` rule over the diff — reused via its `scope: ["tree","diff"]`.
Plan the crawl's `unnamed-predicate` rule over the diff — reused via its `scope: ["tree","diff"]`.

phases.description: One dispatch per planned unit, `role_id: "reviewer"` — the SAME `crawl.unit` kind `crawl.json`'s own `crawl` phase uses, dispatching a different role because #2310 P4c made the role a Task property the kind reads rather than a hardcoded `"crawler"`.
This run's totals, read back through every `crawl.unit` step's own outcome — the SAME `crawl.summary` kind `crawl.json` uses.

tasks.description: Total this review's units, findings and tokens.

phases.description: **#2310 P4e: the coder seat here is a hook, not a dispatch.** Measured 2026-09-05, local coder seats wrote an applying unified diff 1/4, 0/3 and 1/10 times across three seats where a clean-context frontier session wrote 4/4 — so mod CREATION moved off the local tier while DETECTION (the `review` phase's units) stays local. darkmux still never calls a frontier model itself: the hooks sink already fires on `dispatch.tool` + `payload.tool_name == \"create_finding\"` + `payload.ok == true`, the operator's orchestrator session watches those matches, invokes the bundled `darkmux-mod-create` skill, and the skill's subagent records the mod with the ordinary `darkmux mod create --for <key>` verb. This task's job is therefore to WAIT for that mod, bounded, and then gate it — so its first step is a Tier-1 `procedural.shell` poll of `mod list --for` (no `role_id`, no dispatch, no model), and the create-mod MESSAGE that used to live here is gone. `crawl.json`'s own create-mods task is UNTOUCHED and still dispatches a coder (crawl is separate by doctrine), which is why the two configs no longer share one create-mod message. The gate step and the `deliver` phase are unchanged: `mods.gate` takes `{{item.tree_root}}` as its `workdir`, resolves the single source checkout under it, copies that checkout to a scratch dir, `git apply`s the mod's kit there and runs `test_command` inside the PATCHED copy (mods_gate.rs L193-202, L305-306), recording `gate_passed`/`gate_skipped_reason` on every mod naming this task's finding; `deliver.github_review` renders a gate-passed mod as an inline suggestion and everything else as a question. **`mod_wait_seconds` defaults to `0` — do not wait** — so the unattended CI path (no orchestrator session, no frontier seat on the runner) delivers detections without burning a per-finding wait; an attended run opts in with `--param mod_wait_seconds=<N>`. The outer bound on the poll is `runtime.step_command_timeout_seconds`, which `procedural.shell` applies to every step command. **(#2310 P4f) A SECOND way to staff this seat ships beside the first, off:** `create-mod-dispatch` dispatches a `coder` to a HOSTED ENDPOINT profile (`--param mod_seat_profile=<profile>`) instead of waiting, for the unattended self-hosted runner where there is no orchestrator session to receive the hook and therefore nothing a wait could wait for. It carries the byte-identical create-mod message `crawl.json` carries, because it is the same job — what changed is the TIER of the seat reading it, which is exactly what the measurement above found to matter. The two templates `excludes` each other: exactly one may be enabled, both enabled is a validate-time Error naming both, and the dry-run graph shows whichever one is live because the other is pruned at mint. Data boundary: the endpoint seat sends the finding and the source it names off the machine, so it is for PUBLIC repositories only.

tasks.display_name: Await mod: the frontier proposes the change one finding describes
tasks.description: Wait, bounded, for a mod naming this finding, then gate it — one task per entry in the summary's `finding_refs`. No model runs in this task; the mod comes from the operator's frontier monitor (see the phase description).

config.command:
set -eu
key='{{item.key}}'
bound='{{mod_wait_seconds}}'
case "$bound" in
  ''|*[!0-9]*)
    printf 'mod_wait_seconds must be a whole number of seconds, got %s\n' "'$bound'" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
if [ "$bound" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf '{"waited":false,"found":false,"for":"%s","reason":"mod_wait_seconds=0, no frontier monitor expected"}\n' "$key"
  exit 0
fi
elapsed=0
while :; do
  if "${DARKMUX_BIN:-darkmux}" mod list --for "$key" --json 2>/dev/null | grep -q '"key"'; then
    printf '{"waited":true,"found":true,"for":"%s","waited_seconds":%s}\n' "$key" "$elapsed"
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ "$elapsed" -ge "$bound" ]; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 5
  elapsed=$((elapsed + 5))
done
printf 'no mod names %s after %ss; delivering it as a question\n' "$key" "$bound" >&2
printf '{"waited":true,"found":false,"for":"%s","waited_seconds":%s}\n' "$key" "$elapsed"
exit 0

tasks.display_name: Create mod: a cloud seat proposes the change one finding describes
tasks.description: The UNATTENDED way to staff the same seat `create-mod` staffs (#2310 P4f): a `coder` dispatch on a HOSTED ENDPOINT profile, for the self-hosted runner that runs `darkmux-review.yml` on every PR and has no orchestrator session to receive the hook. Ships `"enabled": false` and `excludes: ["create-mod"]` — the two templates are two ways to staff ONE slot, so exactly one is ever live and enabling both is a validate-time Error naming both (see `TaskConfig::excludes`). To use it, copy this document to `~/.darkmux/mission-configs/review-v2.json` and flip the two `enabled` fields: `true` here, `false` on `create-mod`. The seat is pinned with `--param mod_seat_profile=<an endpoint profile name>`; leaving it unset drops the `profile_name` key entirely (a declared-but-uncollected whole-value placeholder omits its key — `mission_config::inputs`) and the dispatch resolves the `coder` role through the machine's own `role_profiles.coder` binding, which is the other way a runner staffs this. The MESSAGE is byte-identical to `crawl.json`'s create-mod message and pinned as such by a test: it is the same job (read the finding, write the smallest applying diff, call `create_mod`), and the kit-shape clauses are what the measurement in DESIGN.md's "the seat boundary is a hook" showed local seats failing. A hosted frontier-class endpoint is the seat that passed. Data boundary: this sends the finding and the file it names to a third-party endpoint, so it is for PUBLIC repositories only. The gate step is the same `mods.gate` the wait template ends with, under its own id (step ids are unique document-wide).

config.message:
A finding recorded earlier in this run is appended below. Your job is to PROPOSE the change that finding describes, as a mod. The workspace you have been given is the tree the finding was observed in, mounted read-only: you cannot edit it, and you are not meant to.

1. Read the file the finding names, around the line it names.
2. If the finding does not hold against what you read, record nothing and say why.
3. Otherwise write the smallest change that resolves it as a unified diff against the file as it is, and call `create_mod` with: `kit` = one sentence saying what to apply, then the exact diff; `for` = the finding's key exactly as the block below spells it.

The diff is applied by a program, so its shape matters:
- File paths relative to the repository root, exactly as the finding's `file` field spells them (`--- a/src/x.ts` / `+++ b/src/x.ts`), never the mount path.
- Context lines copied exactly as they appear in the file you read; one hunk per changed region.
- The diff as plain text, not inside a code fence, and the kit must end with a newline.

Do not run tests, and do not touch anything the finding does not name. The mod is your product; someone else integrates it.

phases.description: #2310 P4c-2b closes the gap the `create-mods` phase's own description names: `records.gather` reads THIS mission's own finding/mod stores (scoped by mission id — the way `finding list --mission`/`mod list --mission` resolve it) plus `diff_file`, into the typed shape `deliver.github_review` renders. Two steps of ONE task, `records-gather-step` then `deliver-step` — the SAME same-task-predecessor `Step.output` -> `input` wiring (`scheduler::gather_inputs`) every other multi-step task in this codebase uses, never a new mechanism. `run_on: ["complete","error"]` on the task documents the intent DESIGN.md's own retirement finding names ("an errored run rendered nothing... None were in a step") — an errored `create-mods` phase must not silence delivery; this task declares no `depends_on` at all (an edge naming `create-mod`, a grow TEMPLATE, is refused at validation — see `mission_config::interpret`'s own doc), so ordering comes from `create-mods` being an earlier PHASE in this document, the same phase-ordering `crawl.json`'s `summarize` phase relies on to see every grown `crawl.unit`'s results with no `depends_on` of its own.

tasks.description: Gather then deliver — see this phase's own description.
